messages:
Sanjay: seeing a big gap in k8s node/gpu metrics from us-east-1, autoscaler is not reacting, requests are piling up on dedicated pools
Maria: confirmed — prometheus scrape errors started ~1763501000, node-exporter timeouts
Alex: autoscaler logs show `missing_node_count` warnings and then a silence. maybe metrics aggregator dropped a label?
Ingrid: can we fail traffic to us-west? dedicated only has limited spare capacity there but should hold for a bit.
Priya: +1 on shifting. I'm prepping a weighted routing change (GSLB) to send 30% -> us-west now, 100% if needed.
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-54: "k8s metrics dropout causing degraded autoscaling - us-east-1" :rotating_light:
Maria: digging into prometheus, the scrape target list shrank. `kube-state-metrics` endpoints for several node pools stopped exposing `node_unschedulable` and `gpu_count` labels.
Sanjay: curious if it's exporter or network egress issue. are we seeing any ENI rate limits or cloud-control-plane errors?
Alex: cloud control plane shows 429s for the metrics pull endpoint from our metrics-aggregator cluster (throttling). saw bursts at 1763500900-1763501100.
Tim: throttling would explain missing metrics. autoscaler relies on `prom_query:sum(gpu_allocated)` which returned 0 for some pools. need fallback to kube API.
Priya: routing change in flight: `gslb set-weight redwood-dedicated-us-east 70` -> ok, now 65/35, watch LB logs.
Ingrid: ops, start draining the most impacted pools after we confirm failover. prefer graceful drain to avoid evicting long-running tasks.
Maria: quick fix: I'm reconfiguring the metrics-aggregator to backoff less aggressively and add retries. patching MON-4321 now.
Alex: for a short-term patch, can we add a synthetic exporter that queries the kube API for node/gpu counts and pushes to prometheus as `synthetic_node_gpu_total`? then autoscaler can use that metric if primary is down.
Sanjay: good idea, make it a low-latency check. I'll spin up a fast lambda to call `/api/v1/nodes` and emit metrics to pushgateway.
Priya: traffic shifted to 55/45 now. latency is rising slightly in us-west but still within SLO.
ops-bot: deploy bot: created deploy pipeline `metrics-aggregator/retry-tuning` by Maria (deploy queued)
Maria: deployed retry tuning to aggregator (v2). Prom scrapes are recovering for ~10% of targets.
Tim: autoscaler health: `kubectl get hpa -A` shows some HPAs still in pending because prometheus queries return NaN. adding fallback to direct API in the controller would avoid this class of outage. filing INFRA-2713.
Ingrid: agree on fallback and also we need better visibility when scrapes are throttled vs exporter errors. current alerts just say 'metric missing' which is hard to triage.
Alex: logging snippet from aggregator: ```2026-03-18T14:12:01Z WARN http_request.go:120 throttled: 429 response: rate exceeded```
Sanjay: we're also missing traces for autoscaler decisions — Jaeger has gaps because samplers drop when DB writes fail. adds to confusion during incidents.
Maria: follow-up list: 1) quick synthetic exporter + pushgateway (Sanjay) 2) autoscaler fallback to kube API (Tim) 3) aggregator retry/backoff fix (done) 4) enhance alerts to distinguish 'scrape throttle' vs 'exporter down' (Ingrid) 5) postmortem + cost analysis for cross-region failover (Alex)
Priya: can we add a temporary quota alert to avoid uncontrolled failover costs? when we route >50% cross-region we should trigger a cost ops notification.
Ingrid: yes, add a pager for cost-ops/channel when gslb weight crosses 50% for >5m. ticketed MON-4329.
ops-bot: pager duty: escalation sent to oncall-team-alpha
Alex: initial impact: degraded autoscaling for ~18 minutes, ~1200 pending requests queued, we shifted 45% traffic -> estimated extra spend ~$1.8k for the hour. will refine numbers in postmortem.
Sanjay: metrics recovered ~1763501400 after retry tuning + partial traffic shift. final routing ended at 70/30 us-east/us-west by 1763501600.
Tim: putting HOTFIX into backlog: embed kube API fallback into autoscaler + add unit tests for missing-metrics scenario. assign INFRA-2713 to me.
Maria: monitoring follow-ups: increase scrapes per second quota in aggregator for control-plane targets, add circuit-breaker metric export, and create a dashboard tracking `scrape_status{reason=~"throttled|timeout|unreachable"}`.
Ingrid: I'll own the post-incident ops checklist and postmortem. target: publish within 72h. POSTMORTEM-2026-07 created.
Priya: reverting GSLB to normal weights now (back to 90/10) as us-east is stable.
ops-bot: incident closed INC-2026-54 (mitigated) :white_check_mark:
Alex: lessons: 1) telemetry throttling is a single-point-of-failure for autoscaling workflows, 2) need synthetic fallbacks, 3) clearer alerts reduce MTTA.
Sanjay: thanks team — will follow up on INFRA-2713 and MON-4329.
Ingrid: adding retro items to the ops board and scheduling a runbook update for region failover with observability checks. :spiral_notepad:
Tim: updated the autoscaler ticket with reproduction steps and a proposed API-fallback patch link: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/autoscaler/pulls/142
Maria: putting a short note in #all-hands about the incident impact and no customer-facing degradation observed.
Priya: closing loop: cost ops notified, postmortem draft expected in ~48h.
Ingrid: good job everyone, closing thread. :thumbsup:"
